name: set_auto_tracing
description: Enable or disable LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation) on ONE existing blockchain address by flipping its enableSniffer flag, without a full-record upsert. Reads the address back first (every writable field, ACTIVE status only) and refuses if it does not exist or is DELETED - this tool never creates a row and never reactivates a DELETED one. Writes back the exact same record with only enableSniffer changed: entityId, type, subType, description, reference and isPublicInfo are preserved verbatim, and the provenance fields (originAddress, previousAddress, txHash, txBlockchain, txTimestamp) are left completely untouched. Returns {before, after} snapshots of the address. Use this instead of create_address to flip the flag.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

network.description: Address blockchain (must match the address's existing network exactly).

enableSniffer.description: The new value for the enableSniffer flag.

name: create_address
description: Add a blockchain address (e.g., '0x...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron) to the Label Cloud, or upsert an existing one. Optional entityId must be a UUID from search_entities, not an entity name. THIS IS A FULL UPSERT: every call replaces the whole record. To flip ONLY the enableSniffer flag (LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation)) on an address that already exists, use set_auto_tracing instead - it reads the record back and preserves every other field for you. To change any other single field on an existing address, you MUST first call search_addresses on it with fields including entityId, description, type, subType, reference, enableSniffer, originAddress, previousAddress, txHash, txBlockchain, txTimestamp, then resend this call with every one of those values carried over unchanged plus only your intended change. Never omit entityId on an existing address that has one: an omitted/absent entityId is written as a literal null, which detaches the address from its entity and forces the address to become publicly visible in the public blacklist. `type` is required and effectively controls severity on the fast path - never guess it; always use the exact value read back from search_addresses, not a paraphrase.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

isPublicInfo.description: Whether address is public or not

entityId.description: Entity UUID (format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx). Get this from search_entities response 'id' field, not the entity name.

enableSniffer.description: Whether the sniffer should watch this address, independent of type/severity. Absent on write = preserve stored value; null = clear. Always a boolean on read (null reads as false).

originAddress.description: Root address a propagated label originated from. Absent on write = preserve stored value; null = clear.

previousAddress.description: Immediate parent address this label propagated from. Part of the provenance quartet (previousAddress/txHash/txBlockchain/txTimestamp): must be all present, all explicitly null, or all absent together.

txHash.description: On-chain transaction hash that carried the propagation.

txTimestamp.description: On-chain transaction time (ISO-8601), NOT the label write time (createdAt).

name: search_addresses
description: Search for a specific blockchain address by its hash (e.g., '0x...' or 'T...'). Cannot search by entity name - use search_entities for that. Pass fields (e.g. enableSniffer, originAddress, previousAddress, txHash, txBlockchain, txTimestamp, publicInfo, organization, entityId, description, type, subType, reference) to read back the full record - required before using create_address to upsert any other field on an existing address, since that call is a full-record write. To read just the LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation) flag and its provenance, use get_auto_tracer_data instead. To flip the flag alone, use set_auto_tracing instead. The response always carries a top-level `tags` array of `{network, tag}` beside publicBlacklist/privateBlacklist. It covers all networks, or only the `blockchains` you pass. It is empty when the address has no tags or is not visible to your key. It is returned whatever `fields` you pass, and also for an address that has tags but no labels (empty lists plus tags). Tag lookup is case-sensitive on the address: send the address in the exact letter case you tagged it with, and pass only non-EVM networks in `blockchains` (any EVM network there makes the lookup lowercase the address). An `incident.*` tag shows only when your key can see both the address and the incident. The tag of a DELETED incident shows only to the incident's owner org and to global read keys. If the incident lookup fails the call returns a 5xx error, never the tag. To list the incidents an address is tagged with (full incident objects), use get_address_incidents. Add or remove tags with add_address_tag / remove_address_tag.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

entityId.description: Entity UUID (format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx). Get this from search_entities response 'id' field, not the entity name.

fields.description: Address fields, default: address, network, description, type, subType, reference, fileLink

name: get_auto_tracer_data
description: Read LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation) data for one address: the enableSniffer flag plus its five provenance fields (originAddress, previousAddress, txHash, txBlockchain, txTimestamp) - without naming any `fields` yourself. Input is just address and an optional network. Its response also carries the address's top-level `tags` array, as search_addresses returns it, limited to `network` when you pass one. Use search_addresses instead if you need other fields such as description, type, subType, reference or entityId.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

name: delete_address
description: Remove an address from the AMLBot Label Cloud

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

name: add_address_tag
description:
Add ONE tag to a blockchain address on one network in the Label Cloud (e.g. `geo.uk.london`, `deposit.binance`). A tag is an extra fact about the address, separate from its label type, and an address can carry many.

**Tag format:** the tag must match `^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$` and be 1-128 characters long: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, with dots separating namespaces (`<namespace>.<value>[.<value>…]`). Anything else, including uppercase or spaces, is rejected with API error 400 and is never converted, so send the tag already lowercase. The one exception is a `.` or `..` piece (e.g. `..` or `a/..`), which is rejected locally with `Invalid path parameter` before any request is sent.

**No edit:** to change a tag, remove the old one with remove_address_tag, then add the new one. Adding a tag the address already has changes nothing and returns `added:false`.

**Network:** `network` is required. EVM addresses are stored lowercased under network `evm_eoa`, so all EVM chains share one tag set. The response echoes the stored address and network.

**Privacy:** tags follow the address's privacy. You can tag an address only if its labels are visible to your key, or if it has no labels at all. Otherwise you get API error 404.

**Reserved `incident` namespace:** a tag that starts with `incident.` is accepted only if an ACTIVE incident with exactly that tag exists and is visible to your key (see create_incident, search_incidents, get_incident_by_tag). Otherwise you get API error 404, indistinguishable from the hidden-address 404. Never compose an incident tag by hand: copy the `tag` of the incident.

**Labels are separate:** tags never change the address's label, and create_address and set_auto_tracing never read, send or clear tags. Read tags back with search_addresses, in its top-level `tags` array.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

tag.description: Tag, 1-128 characters, matching ^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$ (lowercase letters, digits, underscores; dots separate namespaces). Sent verbatim, never lowercased or converted.

name: remove_address_tag
description:
PERMANENTLY remove ONE tag from a blockchain address on one network. This is a hard delete: the tag disappears from every read, and only the audit log keeps a record. There is no undo other than adding it again with add_address_tag. There is also no edit: to change a tag, remove the old one and add the new one.

The address, network and tag rules are the same as add_address_tag: the tag must match `^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$`, be 1-128 characters and be lowercase; EVM addresses are matched lowercased under `evm_eoa`.

**On success** the tool returns `null`.

**API error 404** means one of three things, deliberately indistinguishable because tags follow the address's privacy: the tag is not on the address, the address is not visible to your key, or the tag is an `incident.*` tag of an incident your key cannot see. One exception: the tag of a DELETED incident stays on its addresses and can still be removed by the incident's owner org or by a `write_address_global` key.

**Labels are untouched:** this never removes or changes the address's label. Use delete_address for that.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

tag.description: Tag, 1-128 characters, matching ^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$ (lowercase letters, digits, underscores; dots separate namespaces). Sent verbatim, never lowercased or converted.

name: get_entity_addresses
description: Get all blockchain addresses associated with an entity. Requires entityId (UUID from search_entities), not the entity name.

entityId.description: Entity UUID (format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx). Get this from search_entities response 'id' field, not the entity name.

fields.description: Address fields, default: address, network, description, type, subType, reference, fileLink

name: get_addresses_by_origin
description: Every address a red label propagated to from an origin address, as a complete edge list - every row where originAddress matches, ordered txTimestamp ASC then address ASC. Each edge carries address, previousAddress, txHash, txBlockchain, txTimestamp. Org-blind: returns edges across all organizations, not just the caller's own. limit defaults to 10000 (max 10000), offset defaults to 0; offset is applied after an exhaustive, service-side sort of the whole partition, so cost scales with partition size, not with offset. Part of LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation).

limit.description: Max rows returned (default 10000, max 10000). offset is applied AFTER an exhaustive, service-side-sorted read of the whole origin partition - it is not a cheap deep-paging primitive, and the cost is proportional to partition size, not to offset.

offset.description: Rows to skip after sorting by txTimestamp ASC, address ASC (default 0).

name: get_addresses_by_previous
description: The direct children of one address in a propagation tree (branch isolation) - only the edges whose previousAddress matches, not the whole subtree beneath it. Same five-field edge shape, ordering, limit/offset defaults, and org-blind scope as get_addresses_by_origin. Part of LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation).

limit.description: Max rows returned (default 10000, max 10000). offset is applied AFTER an exhaustive, service-side-sorted read of the whole previous-address partition - it is not a cheap deep-paging primitive, and the cost is proportional to partition size, not to offset.

offset.description: Rows to skip after sorting by txTimestamp ASC, address ASC (default 0).

name: create_entity
description: Create a new entity in the AMLBot Label Cloud. Returns the created entity including its 'id' (UUID) for use in other operations.

isPublicInfo.description: Whether entity is public or not

name: search_entities
description: Search for entities by name. Returns entity details including the 'id' field (UUID) needed for other entity operations like get_entity_addresses.

fields.description: Entity fields, default: description, type, subType, reference

name: get_entity
description: Get entity details by UUID. Use search_entities first to find the entityId if you only have the name.

entityId.description: Entity UUID (format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx). Get this from search_entities response 'id' field, not the entity name.

name: delete_entity
description: Delete an entity by UUID. Use search_entities first to find the entityId if you only have the name.

entityId.description: Entity UUID (format: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx). Get this from search_entities response 'id' field, not the entity name.

name: create_incident
description:
Create an incident: a named event (e.g. a hack) whose tag can be put on many addresses with add_address_tag. Required: `name` and `incidentDate` (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional: `isPublicInfo` (default false), `description`, `reference`, `tag`. Returns the incident including its `id` (UUID, for get_incident / update_incident / delete_incident / get_incident_addresses) and its `tag`.

**Tag:** omit `tag` to have it generated as `incident.<slug>.<yyyymmdd>`. An explicit `tag` must match `^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$`, be at most 128 characters, and its date part must equal `incidentDate` written as yyyymmdd; otherwise API error 400 and nothing is stored. The tag is immutable (settable on create only) and is never reused: a duplicate, including the tag of a DELETED incident, gives API error 409.

**Public vs private:** `isPublicInfo: true` needs a `write_address_global` key (otherwise API error 403). A private incident is visible to your organization only. Unknown fields give API error 400.

**Membership:** to put an address on the incident, call add_address_tag with the incident's exact `tag`. Incident tags are copied by LabelSniffer (a.k.a. auto-tracer, a.k.a. auto-label-propagation) onto the addresses it labels. LabelSniffer carries only public incidents and private incidents owned by the org `amlbot`.

isPublicInfo.description: Public incidents need write_address_global. Default false (private to the owner organization).

tag.description: Explicit tag incident.<slug>.<yyyymmdd>; its date part must equal incidentDate. Generated from name when absent.

name: get_incident
description: Get one incident by its UUID `id` (from create_incident, search_incidents or get_incident_by_tag). Returns {id, name, tag, organization, isPublicInfo, description, incidentDate, reference, status, createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy}. API error 404 when it does not exist or is not visible to your key.

incidentId.description: Incident UUID. Get this from the `id` field of create_incident, search_incidents or get_incident_by_tag, not the incident name or tag.

name: get_incident_by_tag
description: Get one incident by its exact tag (e.g. `incident.binance_hack.20261030`). Same incident object as get_incident. The tag is sent verbatim. A DELETED incident is still returned to its owner org and to global keys, with `status: DELETED`. API error 404 when no incident holds that tag or it is not visible to your key.

name: search_incidents
description: List incidents visible to your key. Optional filters: `name`, `status` (ONE of ACTIVE or DELETED, default ACTIVE), `isPublicInfo`. `limit` is 1-100 (default 50). Returns `{items, nextCursor}`. Pages may be short or even empty before the end of the list: ALWAYS pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is null, and only then treat the list as complete.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from nextCursor. Follow it until nextCursor is null; a page may be short or empty before the end.

name: update_incident
description: Partially update an incident by UUID `id`: send only the fields to change among `name`, `description`, `reference`, `isPublicInfo`; omitted fields stay as they are. The `tag` is immutable and is not an input of this tool. Changing `incidentDate` returns API error 400, because the tag carries the date. Making an incident public needs a `write_address_global` key (API error 403 otherwise). API error 404 when it does not exist or is not visible.

incidentId.description: Incident UUID. Get this from the `id` field of create_incident, search_incidents or get_incident_by_tag, not the incident name or tag.

name: delete_incident
description: Soft-delete an incident by UUID `id`; idempotent. The incident's tag is NOT removed from the addresses it is on and is never reused. A DELETED incident stays visible to its owner org and to global read keys, and its tag can still be removed from addresses with remove_address_tag by the owner org or a `write_address_global` key. Returns `null` on success. API error 403 without permission, 404 when it does not exist or is not visible.

incidentId.description: Incident UUID. Get this from the `id` field of create_incident, search_incidents or get_incident_by_tag, not the incident name or tag.

name: get_incident_addresses
description: List the addresses tagged with an incident (by its UUID `id`). Returns `{items: [{address, network, tag, createdAt, createdBy}], nextCursor}`; `network` is `evm_eoa` for every EVM chain. `limit` is optional. Pages may be short or empty before the end: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` unchanged (it is opaque) until it is null. API error 400 for a bad cursor, 404 when the incident does not exist or is not visible.

incidentId.description: Incident UUID. Get this from the `id` field of create_incident, search_incidents or get_incident_by_tag, not the incident name or tag.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from nextCursor. Follow it until nextCursor is null; a page may be short or empty before the end.

name: get_address_incidents
description: List the incidents an address is tagged with. Input: `address` and an optional `network` filter (EVM chains are normalised to `evm_eoa`). Returns `{items: [{network, tag, incident}]}` where `incident` is the full incident object. An address that is not visible to your key gives `items: []` (HTTP 200), not a 404. API error 500 if an incident lookup fails.

address.description: Blockchain address hash (e.g., '0x1234...' for Ethereum, 'T...' for Tron). Not an entity name.

network.description: Narrow to one network; every EVM chain reads as evm_eoa.

name: get_networks
description: Get list of supported blockchain networks

name: get_types
description: Get list of available address types
